abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions track the app's real variation well and enabled three near-identical detail pages, but the badge markup is half-migrated to its component and the card shape is constructed in two places, inviting drift.

findings.issue: Pokémon-card construction (id→species mapping, humanized name, sprite) is duplicated between getSpeciesMeta (:144) and speciesCardsFromRefs (:173), so a sprite/mapping bug fix must be applied twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared toCard(id, extra) helper (or have getSpeciesMeta reuse speciesCardsFromRefs-style construction) so the species↔Pokémon assumption lives in one place.

findings.issue: TypeBadge is only used inside PokemonCardList; the anchor variant of the badge is copy-pasted as class="type-badge type-{name}" links in four templates (pokemon hero, MovesTable, move page, type relations).
findings.suggestion: Give TypeBadge an optional href prop (or render a snippet) and use it in all six sites, so badge markup changes once.

findings.issue: Each column is described three times: the columns array, the value() switch, and the hardcoded <td> cells; adding a column requires three synchronized edits.
findings.suggestion: Drive the tbody cells from the same column descriptors (key, label, accessor, optional href/type) that drive the thead.

findings.issue: The 150 ms search debounce timer is never cleared when the component unmounts, so a pending timeout can fire a goto() after navigation away.
findings.suggestion: Clear it in an $effect cleanup or on destroy.

findings.issue: {#each sorted as row (row)} keys rows by object identity, so re-sorting remounts every row.
findings.suggestion: Key by stable fields, e.g. (row.moveName + ':' + row.level).

summary: This is a clean, current-idiom SvelteKit 3 / Svelte 5 app: server data access is isolated in one server-only module, all card lists funnel through one component and one shared builder, and the only shared state (filters) lives in the URL using the documented shallow-routing API. Editability is very good overall; the main risks are a duplicated card-construction path, half-adopted TypeBadge abstraction, and MovesTable's triple-described columns.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Delete one route directory plus the spec-mandated Abilities section on the Pokémon page (and its load field). No nav links, no dead helpers, no abilities-only CSS.

scenarios.change: Fix wrong sprite for species whose default Pokémon differs (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: Sprite URL derivation is centralized in spriteUrl (api.js:35) and all lists render via PokemonCardList, so a URL-level fix is one edit. But the id→species card mapping is built in two places (getSpeciesMeta :144, speciesCardsFromRefs :173), so a mapping-level fix must be duplicated or preceded by a refactor; the detail page already models the correct approach via varieties/is_default (pokemon/[name]/+page.server.js:22-24).

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: All four card lists (home, move, ability, type) render through PokemonCardList, so a sort (or sortBy prop) there covers everything; alternatively one edit in speciesCardsFromRefs plus the home page's derived filtered list.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: The data layer (api, error, englishName, latestEnglishFlavor) and the surface/facts CSS classes are directly reusable, and the moves/[name] pattern is a thin template to follow. But /moves has no index route to clone, so the /items list page is a small new build, and there's no generic detail-page abstraction — a modest amount of copying is inevitable.
